newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Erbakan says polls will be democracy test.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Erbakan says polls will be democracy test.

text.p: Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan, locked in a row between his ruling Islamists and the secularist establishment, said on Tuesday that proposed early elections would test Turkey's democracy.
"This will be a referendum on whether there will be respect for the people or a struggle with the people. That is what will be decided," Erbakan told a meeting of his Islam-based Welfare Party MPs.
Erbakan announced last weekend he would go to early elections to solve a dispute over religious activism, which has hamstrung his coalition with pro-Western conservatives.

No date has yet been set for the polling, although a senior member of Erbakan's True Path Party coalition ally said on Monday that polls would be held by the end of this year. A general election would normally be due by 2000.
Erbakan, modern Turkey's first Islamist leader, suggested a plan to swap jobs with his coalition partner, Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller, by the end of June may not be so easy.

He told his MPs that Welfare and Ciller's True Path Party had to fix the timing of the elections and work together to produce election legislation acceptable to parliament before early polls could be held.
"When these conditions are carried out, we will not hesitate to hand over the prime ministership to our coalition partners," Erbakan said.
A joint committee of the two parties met for the first time on Monday to discuss parliamentary procedures in the run up to early elections.
Welfare narrowly won general elections in 1995 with 21 percent of the vote and was helped to power by splits among the secularist parties.
The Islamists say their support has grown since then in a reaction to intense criticism of the government by the secularist army, media and judiciary.
